newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds upside seen capped at 110-22.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds upside seen capped at 110-22.

text.p: June T-bond futures are positive but may find upside gains limited in the short term, with resistance stepping in at 110-22 on Friday, technical analysts said.

"It has got to be bullish for the short term," said Philip Gardiner, technical analyst at Technical Data in London. "Yesterday we went down on inflation data but the speed with which we came back and went on to test the highs was really encouraging."
But he said resistance at 110-22, the high so far this week, should hold on Friday.
"Short-term oscillators are approaching overbought levels and that would support a hold in, so 110-22 is likely to be the maximum for today."
At 1103 GMT, June T-bond futures were up 2/32 at 110-12 in automated trade. The LIFFE June T-bonds contract was also at 110-12, up 15/32 on the day.

Gardiner said the near term technical outlook was backed up by the fundamental picture with little economic data for the market to focus on Friday and ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.
A broker at a European bank in London also saw 110-22 as likely to cap trading on Friday.
"A break through 110-22 would be very bullish, but I can't see it happening today," he said. "Through there it would target the 111-04 area."
The market set a high of 111-04 on Jan 31.
To the downside, he said a pivotal area around 110-00 would support the market.
Gardiner agreed that support would likely hold the market. "I can't see any reason for it to go below there, but if it does 109-22 will be the next prop," he said.
On daily charts 109-22 was the low on May 14.
The European bank trader cited props in a congestion zone of highs and lows from 110-05 down to 109-29.
"The market would have to get back down to 109-16 before there is any decent support," he said.
At the short end, September Eurodollars were at 93.935, up 0.015 on the day.
